lessons.title: Fake frontend / phishing site with a real contract name
lessons.content:
# Fake frontend / phishing site with a real contract name

Attackers do not always invent a new protocol. They invent a **page** that prints a real name, a real hex in the footer, even a real docs link, while the wallet popup asks you to approve a **different spender**. Module 1 said the app is not the protocol. This lesson is the failure case: you believed the paint.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to walk a check that does not trust the footer, and refuse the after-the-fact story “but it had the official contract on the page.” This academy will not send you a DeFi URL in chat.

## What is real, what is theatre

**Real:** bytecode at a hex on a chain you can name. **Theatre:** logos, footers, screenshots of explorers, “verified” badges on the website itself, comment-section links, search ads. A phishing site can iframe a real BscScan page while its JavaScript still packs a hostile approve.

Wallet connection is not the theft. The theft is the signature: approve the wrong spender, or swap through the wrong router, or sign typed data that sets allowance without a second pop you understand. Seed-phrase phishing is the Basic-course cousin. Intermediate DeFi phishing often never asks for the seed. It asks for a signature you have been trained to tap quickly.

Staff of this academy will never send a “connect to verify your homework” link. They will never ask for a seed, a key, or 2FA.

## Where the fakes live

Search ads above the real domain. Misspelled domains. In-app browsers opened from a message. Bookmarks that were rewritten by malware. Copies of the real UI with one extra approve. “Support” pop-ups after a failed transaction. All of these attack the app layer because the app layer is cheaper to fake than a verified-on-chain pool with actual inventory.

TABLE
What you saw | What you must still check | If you skip it
Official name in the title | Domain spelling versus a source you already had | You connect to a clone
Real hex in the footer | Spender hex in the wallet pop versus explorer | Footer was wallpaper
Iframe of BscScan | URL bar of the explorer you typed | You read a picture of an explorer
“WalletConnect to continue” | Whether you needed to continue at all | Session plus a later hostile request
ENDTABLE

## The check, boring on purpose

Type the explorer from a bookmark. Paste the router or pool hex from a document you obtained without the suspect page. Confirm bytecode. Then, when the wallet pops, compare the `to` or spender to that hex, start and end, on the correct chain ID. If the site needed you to be in a hurry, that is a finding.

Trust Wallet and MetaMask — examples of wallet apps — will show what they are asked to show. They are not detectives. They will sign a hostile approve with the same calm as an honest one.

Crystal Stones’ published hex in a fake “CS DeFi” footer is a favourite costume. The hex `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` is verify-only. It is not a farm. A page that says “approve CS to the official router” while the spender is random is this lesson. Tuition is **$10 USDT BEP-20 through academy checkout**, never a connect-to-pay DeFi page.

**Worked scenario.** A learner searches a famous AMM name and clicks the first result.

1. The learner does not connect. The learner reads the domain character by character.
2. The learner opens BscScan or Etherscan from a bookmark, not from the result’s button.
3. The learner finds the router hex from a source that is not the ad.
4. If they still use a frontend, they compare the first approve spender to that router.
5. On mismatch, they reject and close the tab. They do not “try a tiny approve to test.”

DIAGRAM
PAGE (theatre)                     POPUP (the book will obey)
+----------------------+           +----------------------+
| real protocol name   |           | spender: 0xBAD...    |
| real hex in footer   |           | token: USDT          |
| iframe of explorer   |           | amount: UNLIMITED    |
+----------------------+           +----------------------+
LEFT can be honest or cloned. RIGHT is the only object the token program will honour.
ENDDIAGRAM

## After a bad connect

Disconnect the session. It does not revoke. Read allowance. Revoke if a spender you do not want is live. Move remaining tokens if you believe the key might also be compromised — different wound. Do not DM “recovery.” Recovery is theft in a high-vis jacket.

NOTE
Academy rule: a real name on a fake page is still a fake page. Compare spender hexes. We will not send you DeFi links. We will not ask for a seed to “check if the site was real.”
ENDNOTE

## What this lesson is for

You can now treat a familiar name as a costume until the popup matches the book. Next: unlimited approve to a hostile spender — when the debit order is the whole attack.

## Say this out loud

- A phishing DeFi site can print a real contract name and still request a different spender.
- The wallet popup is what the chain will obey, not the footer.
- Search ads and hurry are part of the design of the scam, not a coincidence.
- Disconnect is not revoke; read allowance after a scare.
- Academy staff will not DM a DeFi URL or ask for a seed.

Next: unlimited approve to a hostile spender — the debit order that waits.

lessons.title: Unlimited approve to a hostile spender
lessons.content:
# Unlimited approve to a hostile spender

The Ethereum course called approve a standing debit order. DeFi makes that order the usual first tap. A **hostile spender** is a contract (or an EOA) that will call `transferFrom` when it is ready — not when you tap swap. Unlimited allowance is how one signature donates every current and future unit of that token at that address.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to describe a drain that happens hours later, say why a zero balance was not safety, and refuse “set spending cap to max” as a default. This academy will not tell you to approve anyone.

## The later pull is the point

A simple thief asks for the seed now. A DeFi thief asks for unlimited USDT to 0xBAD, lets you complete a small swap from a nested honest pool (or fakes a success toast), and returns when your balance is fatter. Payroll lands. A friend refunds you. You bridge in. `transferFrom` runs. The explorer shows a successful token transfer from you to them, authorised by the allowance you wrote.

You will not see a new website pop if they already have the allowance. Your wallet can look idle. Idle is not revoked.

If the spender is a contract with a hidden `drain` called by its owner, the owner waits. If the spender is an EOA you approved by mistake (rare in honest UX, common in hostile calldata), that EOA can pull whenever.

## Unlimited plus refill is a loop

Revoke stops the loop. Sending the remaining tokens to a new EOA without revoking leaves the old address dangerous for the next inbound transfer. Hiding the token in the wallet UI does nothing. Approving a second “cleaner” contract from a recovery ad is often a second hostile spender.

TABLE
What you did | What the hostile spender can do | What actually stops it
Unlimited approve | Pull until empty, now or later | Revoke, or empty forever and abandon the address
Exact approve of 50 | Pull up to 50 | Cap already small; still revoke if hostile
Zero balance, leftover unlimited | Pull the next inbound units | Revoke before you refill
New EOA, old allowance untouched | Pull from the old EOA | Do not send to the old EOA
ENDTABLE

## How the popup hides max

Some wallets show “unlimited” in words. Some show a huge integer. Some show the token amount you typed for the swap while calldata still has max uint. Read the decoded allowance if present. If the wallet cannot decode, you are signing blind. Blind plus max is how this wound is inflicted on careful people.

Permit signatures (typed data) can set the same unlimited allowance without a classic approve transaction. Read spender and amount in that message too. A permit for a hostile spender is not gentler because it did not show a gas bar.

Crystal Stones unlimited approve to a mystery spender is the same wound on a BEP-20. Do not approve CS to “activate” anything. The published hex is not a spender you pay. Checkout is **$10 USDT BEP-20 through academy checkout**. Staff will not ask you to approve a cleaner.

**Worked scenario.** A learner swapped a small amount of USDT a month ago. Today USDT leaves while they are offline.

1. The learner opens the token’s explorer page and reads the outgoing `transferFrom`.
2. The learner notes the spender and finds the old Approval event with a max value.
3. The learner revokes that spender on every token they approved if they still control the key.
4. The learner does not sign a new “refund contract.”
5. The learner treats remaining assets as hot until allowances are zero and they decide whether the key is still only theirs.

DIAGRAM
DAY 0                              DAY 30
+------------------+               +------------------+
| approve UNLIMITED|               | inbound +80 USDT |
| swap 15 USDT     |               | spender pulls 80 |
| balance looks ok |               | toast: none      |
+------------------+               +------------------+
Same debit order. Later inventory. The book is consistent.
ENDDIAGRAM

## Practice size limits the blast

If you never keep more on a hot EOA than you can lose, a later pull is a lesson instead of a hole in the month. That is not victim-blaming. That is how you live with standing orders on a public computer. Split addresses if you must: one EOA for experiments with tiny inventories, one that never approves DeFi spenders.

NOTE
Academy rule: unlimited is a memory. Hostile spenders use time. Revoke when the job is done. Exact caps if you must approve. Never grant a spender because a refund was promised.
ENDNOTE

## What this lesson is for

You can now see a delayed drain as the same approve you already understood. Next: wrong-chain DeFi — the book was never the one you meant.

## Say this out loud

- A hostile spender can pull later; unlimited allowance is the invitation.
- Zero balance does not kill a max allowance.
- Permit can set the same debit order without a classic approve tx.
- Recovery “cleaners” are often a second hostile spender.
- This academy will not ask you to approve a contract to pay or to refund.

Next: wrong-chain “DeFi” — same letters, different book, missing inventory.

lessons.title: Wrong-chain “DeFi”
lessons.content:
# Wrong-chain “DeFi”

The website says Ethereum. The wallet is on BNB Smart Chain, or the reverse. The ticker says USDT. The contract is a copy on the other book — or nothing useful. You approve, you swap, you add liquidity, and you have interacted with a **different set of programs**. Intermediate already taught two books. This is the DeFi-shaped way to ignore that lesson.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to name chain ID, explorer, fuel, and token contracts as a preflight, and describe what “the funds vanished” usually means when the letters matched. This academy will not tell you to bridge as a fix.

## Same letters are not a bridge

Your EOA address looks identical on chain 1 and chain 56. Pools do not. Routers do not. USDT does not. A frontend can switch the wallet’s network in the background after you connected, or it can fail to switch and still draw Ethereum logos. If you signed while the wallet network badge said BSC, you paid BNB to talk to BSC programs, even if the tab’s CSS was Ethereum-coloured.

Copycat tokens love the wrong-chain moment. You meant wrapped ether on Ethereum. You approved a “WETH” BEP-20 that a stranger minted this morning. The pool was liquid in that fake WETH because the stranger filled both sides. You swapped honest USDT into trash. k held. The book was consistent. You still lost.

## Bridging is another program, not a undo button

If you sent the right token on the wrong chain to a contract that does not exist there, you may have written into a well. A **bridge** is extra programs plus extra custodians or extra verifiers. This course will not teach a bridge workflow. It will say: **do not bridge in a panic to “recover” a wrong-chain DeFi tap.** Panic-bridges are how people pay a second hostile app.

Exchange withdrawals have the same geography. Binance, as an example of a CEX, asks which network. If you withdraw USDT-ERC20 to a wallet you only use on BSC DeFi, you now hold a row on Ethereum. BSC routers cannot spend it. Fuel on BSC (BNB) will not move Ethereum USDT.

TABLE
What you intended | What you signed | Usual result
Ethereum pool | Chain 56 tx | BSC copycat or empty contract; ETH never moved
BSC USDT | Ethereum USDT contract | Different notebook; router reverts or takes the other USDT
WBNB | WETH letters | Fake token or wrong wrapped native
Academy $10 BEP-20 | ETH on chain 1 | Checkout not paid; ETH spent elsewhere
ENDTABLE

## Preflight is four names

Before any DeFi signature: **chain ID, native fuel, explorer, token/router hexes.** Read them on the wallet badge and on the explorer you typed. If the frontend cannot wait for that, you do not need that frontend.

Crystal Stones lives on BSC as the published BEP-20. A “CS DeFi” site that asks for Ethereum ETH gas is already wrong-chain theatre unless they independently deployed a different token — which would not be the asset this academy verifies. Do not send CS cross-chain to chase a farm. Do not pay tuition on the wrong book. **Checkout is $10 USDT BEP-20 through academy checkout.**

**Worked scenario.** A learner’s swap succeeded on the explorer they finally opened — BscScan — but they thought they were on Ethereum.

1. The learner reads chain ID 56 on the tx.
2. The learner lists which token contracts were pulled — BSC hexes.
3. The learner does not send ETH to “complete the bridge.”
4. The learner revokes BSC spenders they did not mean to keep.
5. The learner, if they still need an Ethereum action, starts from zero on chain 1 with ETH for gas and Ethereum token contracts.

DIAGRAM
INTENDED                            SIGNED
+------------------+               +------------------+
| chain 1          |               | chain 56         |
| ETH fuel         |               | BNB fuel         |
| Ethereum USDT    |               | BSC USDT or fake |
| Ethereum router  |               | BSC router       |
+------------------+               +------------------+
Logos can match. Books do not. The signed column is the history.
ENDDIAGRAM

## Explorers do not gossip across books

Etherscan will not show your BSC swap. BscScan will not show your Ethereum approve. Opening the “wrong” explorer and seeing nothing is not a refund. It is the other library’s silence. Bookmark both. Use the one that matches the wallet badge.

NOTE
Academy rule: wrong-chain DeFi is not a bridge request. It is a signed history on the book you actually used. Name four things before the signature. Do not pay a panic-bridge.
ENDNOTE

## What this lesson is for

You can now treat network badges as part of the contract, not as chrome. Next: rug as a function — pull liquidity, admin mint — not as a vibe.

## Say this out loud

- Address letters matching does not move inventories across chain 1 and chain 56.
- Frontends can wear the wrong chain’s paint while the wallet signs the other book.
- Fake wrapped tokens thrive in wrong-chain moments.
- Bridging in a panic is a second program, not an undo.
- Crystal Stones verification is a BSC BEP-20, not an Ethereum farm.

Next: rug as pull-liquidity or admin mint — a function, not a mood.

lessons.title: Rug as pull-liquidity / admin mint, not a vibe
lessons.content:
# Rug as pull-liquidity / admin mint, not a vibe

A **rug** in this course is not “bad vibes” and not “the team was rude.” It is a **function that extracts the honest side of a pool or inflates a token** so that remaining holders sit on empty shelves or diluted rows. Typical shapes: `removeLiquidity` by an insider who held most LP tokens; a privileged `mint`; a pause that traps you while the insider exits; a proxy upgrade that points at drain bytecode.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to name those functions, know what “renounced” would have to mean on the explorer, and refuse rug as a personality test. This academy will not call a project a rug for you as a service.

## Pull-liquidity is a remove by someone who owns the receipt

If a deployer adds liquidity, holds the LP tokens, and later burns them for almost all of both shelves, the pool’s x and y collapse. Your remaining LP share is a share of dust. k still “worked.” Traders who bought the token on the way up were swapping against shelves the deployer still owned. **Who holds the LP supply** is the question. A lock contract can hold it. A lock can be fake. A lock can expire. Read the LP holder list on the explorer, not a padlock emoji.

Honey-pot variants: you can buy, but token code blocks your sell. That is a token-program function, not an AMM mood. Read transfer restrictions. You will not audit every token. You will assume a brand-new ticker can block you, and you will not size as if it cannot.

## Admin mint is a printer

If the token owner can mint, they can dump into the pool. x*y=k stays internally consistent while the honest inventory is drained against paper. Verification of source does not remove a mint function. Verification means the compiler matched. Module 1 leftover: a boss is a slot.

TABLE
Rug shape | Function-shaped object | What a vibe story says instead
Pull liquidity | Insider burns LP, shelves collapse | “They rugged because they are bad people”
Admin mint | Privileged mint, then sell into the pool | “Whales dumped”
Pause and trap | pause() while insider exits elsewhere | “Network congestion”
Proxy swap | New implementation drains | “Unexpected vulnerability”
Fake lock | LP sitting at an EOA labelled “lock” | “Liquidity locked, so safe”
ENDTABLE

## Renounced is a fact to read

**Renounce ownership** is a transaction that sets owner to the zero address, if the program actually did that. Tweets are not that transaction. Some programs have a second admin slot. Some “renounce” and keep a mint on a different role. Read. If you cannot read it, you do not have the safety the tweet described.

Crystal Stones’ RWA story is **their claim to verify**, not a rug-rating this academy issues. The hex `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` is for identity on BSC. This course will not tell you to buy CS because it is “not a rug,” and will not tell you to sell because a thread used the word. We teach the functions. We do not run a gossip desk.

Do not send funds to that hex “to be safe from rugs.” That is not how safety works. Tuition is **$10 USDT BEP-20 through academy checkout**.

**Worked scenario.** A learner watches a pool’s BNB inventory collapse in one transaction.

1. The learner opens the tx and looks for a removeLiquidity or a large burn of LP tokens.
2. The learner checks who held that LP supply two blocks before.
3. The learner does not buy the dip as a moral lesson.
4. The learner does not sign a “lawsuit pool” from comments.
5. The learner, if they held LP, attempts remove for whatever dust remains, then stops.

DIAGRAM
BEFORE INSIDER REMOVE              AFTER
+------------------+               +------------------+
| shelves: deep    |               | shelves: dust    |
| LP: mostly insider|              | insider got A+B  |
| your LP: 1%      |               | your 1% of dust  |
+------------------+               +------------------+
The formula kept. The inventory left through a legal call.
ENDDIAGRAM

## “Community token” is not an opposite of rug

A fair-looking distribution can still mint. A mint-free token can still sit in a pool whose LP is unlocked. You need both sides: token privileges and LP custody. Missing either question is how vibe replaces a checklist.

NOTE
Academy rule: rug means a function emptied the honest inventory or printed against it. Name the function. Padlock emojis are not holders. This academy will not be your rumour mill.
ENDNOTE

## What this lesson is for

You can now say rug without a personality story. Last lesson: practice rules that keep you alive around all of the above — including how this course is actually paid for.

## Say this out loud

- A liquidity pull is a remove by whoever holds the LP supply.
- Admin mint can keep k true while emptying the honest side.
- Renounced ownership is an explorer fact, not a tweet.
- Verified source does not delete a mint or a pause.
- Crystal Stones’ hex is verify-only, not a safety deposit box.

Next: practice rules — tiny size, revoke, and academy checkout as USDT BEP-20, not Crystal Stones.

lessons.title: Practice rules (tiny size, revoke, academy checkout is USDT BEP-20 not Crystal Stones)
lessons.content:
# Practice rules (tiny size, revoke, academy checkout is USDT BEP-20 not Crystal Stones)

DeFi is a public computer running swap, pool, and lend without a parent. The only honest practice is **tiny size**, **named chain**, **read then revoke**, and **never mixing tuition with a protocol**. This lesson is the pocket card for the whole course.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to recite the practice rules in your own words, including how Intermediate is paid for, and refuse the last social-engineering costumes. This academy will not tell you to deploy a strategy.

## Tiny size means a loss you already accepted

If a swap, supply, or LP add would change your month, it is not practice. Practice belongs on amounts you can watch vanish. Testnet, where you can get it, is even better: worthless play coins on a practice computer. Mainnet tiny size still burns real gas. Budget the gas as part of the lesson cost.

Split work. An EOA that never approves DeFi spenders can hold the coins you are not experimenting with. An experiment EOA holds fuel plus dust-sized tokens. Mixing those piles is how an unlimited approve becomes a month.

## Revoke is part of the job, not an aftercare product

After a practice swap: read allowance, approve-zero if you do not need the spender, confirm the read is 0. After a practice farm: unstake, remove if you want the base tokens, revoke the farm. After a scare: same reads, no recovery DMs. Fuel must remain for the revoke. Do not spend the last BNB on a third retry.

Staff will never ask for a seed, a private key, 2FA codes, or remote screen control to “finish the revoke for you.”

TABLE
Rule | In practice | Counterfeit version
Tiny size | Dust you can lose | “Tiny” that is still rent
Named chain | Badge, explorer, fuel, hexes | Logo colour
Revoke | approve(0) + re-read | Disconnect, hide token, send CS to a contract
Checkout | $10 USDT BEP-20 via academy checkout | CS token, ETH, chat 0x, pool deposit
Keys | Only you type them, only in the wallet | Staff, support, refund bot
ENDTABLE

## Checkout is not a DeFi action

This Intermediate course costs **$10 USDT on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20)** through **academy checkout** or a **third-party payment processor**. It is not a swap. It is not an approve. It is not a supply. It is not a send to `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00`. That address is the Crystal Stones BEP-20 to **verify**. Verification is not payment. Crystal Stones token is not tuition. ETH on Ethereum is not tuition. A router is not a cashier.

If a page, a person, or a pop-up says otherwise, it is wrong or hostile. This academy will not name a payment vendor. It will name the rail: USDT BEP-20, academy checkout.

**Worked scenario.** A learner finishes Module 6 and wants to keep practising.

1. The learner keeps experiment sizes at dust and keeps a separate EOA without DeFi allowances for anything larger.
2. The learner books Etherscan and BscScan, and reads chain ID before every signature.
3. The learner revokes leftover spenders from this course’s practice, then re-reads allowance.
4. The learner ignores a message: “send CS to the contract to mint your certificate.”
5. The learner, if they still need to pay for access, uses academy checkout in $10 USDT BEP-20 — not a pool, not a farm, not a chat.

DIAGRAM
KEEP                                 DO NOT
+---------------------------+        +---------------------------+
| dust-sized practice       |        | rent on a health factor   |
| named chain + explorer    |        | search-ad frontend        |
| revoke + re-read          |        | unlimited leftover        |
| $10 USDT BEP-20 checkout  |        | CS to 0xe252...           |
| keys stay in your wallet  |        | seed to "support"         |
+---------------------------+        +---------------------------+
ENDDIAGRAM

## What you can say after six modules

DeFi is programs for swap, pool, and lend. Apps lie. Approvals are debit orders. Pools are shelves. Lending is not a bank. LP tokens are receipts. IL is a comparison. Fakes, unlimited spenders, wrong chain, and rugs are functions and costumes, not mysteries. You are not a farmer because you finished a quiz. You are harder to rush.

NOTE
Academy rule: practice is tiny, named, revocable, and separate from tuition. Crystal Stones’ contract is verify-only. Intermediate is $10 USDT BEP-20 through academy checkout. Staff never ask for seed, key, or 2FA.
ENDNOTE

## What this lesson is for

This is the pocket card. You do not need a seventh module of shops. You need the reflex to name the object before you sign.

## Say this out loud

- Practice sizes are amounts I already accepted I can lose.
- After a DeFi job I read allowance and revoke spenders I do not need.
- Academy checkout is $10 USDT BEP-20, not Crystal Stones and not a pool.
- The Crystal Stones hex is verify-only, never a payment address.
- Academy staff never ask for a seed phrase, a private key, or 2FA.

Next: you already have the course. Use it as a brake.
